about: READ-ONLY: does the reader door's socket hand-over hold on this host? `boss probe-door-check`, the tree's CLI installed here from the converged image (backlog e65dde24, from review 991bb439 of car 0e24cda2). A recorded probe reads the system of record through a Unix socket root makes and hands to the probe account (crates/orchestrators/boss-cli/src/probe_reader.rs); the first cut of that hand-over let the account make root chown any file on the host, and the repair's by-effect test needs a root that holds CAP_CHOWN — which the dev pod's root does not, the gate (uid 65534) is not, and this host is, without a cargo to run a test with. So the check ships in the binary and the host runs it on itself, BEFORE any reader credential is deposited here. As root it makes a scratch directory under the temp directory, plants the link an attacker would, hands a socket over with the door's own functions to the account this host NAMES for `boss prove --unattended` (BOSS_PROBE_USER from the runner's drop-in), and reports one line per effect, each judged by what root then finds on disk and never by a command's exit: a command run as each of the two other accounts IS that account (the method's own control, for both); what the planted link points at is still root's; the socket is the account's alone and its directory root's, open to traversal only; AS THE ACCOUNT (runuser under timeout, the door's own way in) it connects and is answered, and cannot plant a link in the directory, replace the socket with a link, remove it, rename it, or rename the directory away; a third account (nobody, else daemon — neither root nor the probe account) cannot connect; and the door's port list (infra/forge/sor-ports.env under BOSS_PROBE_DIR) is root's and closed to group and other, with its owner and mode printed — root sends the reader credential to every port that list names, and nothing had read that file's mode on a host before this line. exit 0 every effect held; 1 one did not — the first is named on a FAIL line and nothing after it is claimed; 2 it could not be checked here (not root, a root that cannot chown, BOSS_PROBE_USER unset — the door's fallback to the checkout's owner is never checked in the probe account's place — no such account, a tool missing), said as REFUSED, which is never a pass. The LAST line is the one verdict, HELD, FAILED or REFUSED, printed after the scratch directory's removal has been judged. It opens no reader credential and no machine token (it never calls the door's open, the only thing that reads one), speaks to no network — the listener behind the socket is its own — and gives the commands it runs as other accounts an empty environment but PATH. NOTHING OUTSIDE THE SCRATCH DIRECTORY IS WRITTEN, and that is held by the code rather than by a kernel setting (review cd3f6a99, B1): the scratch directory stays root's alone to write; its two fixture files are made with an exclusive create that follows no link and refuses a name already there, private from the moment they exist; the only directory other accounts may write in is one inside it, where root makes nothing but door directories under random names, as a door is made in /tmp; a name found already standing is neither written nor removed and ends the run REFUSED or FAILED naming it. A kill mid-run leaves a root-owned boss-probe-door-check-* directory of fixtures under the temp directory. No arguments. No approval: it is a read in this allowlist's sense, the same class as probe-account-controls — it changes no state that outlives it, takes nothing from the filer, and what it reports is what an approver would need in order to decide anything.
